thread:
Jules Park: Heads-up: Quicksilver (onboarding) flagged for potential renewal risk. Their onboarding dashboard shows a recurring latency SLO miss during peak onboarding runs. Need a short packet for the CSM + renewal team explaining: 30d & 90d p95, regional uptime, any fallback usage, incident notes, and a plain-language credit example. Can eng-sre + onboarding ops help assemble?

Ravi Menon: On it. Which service & regions? Also do we want 24h histograms or just percentiles?

Jules Park: Service id = qs-onboard-api. Regions = us-west-2 primary, ap-southeast-1 warm. Percentiles + a 24h heatmap around peak windows would be helpful.

Hannah Liu: I'll take the customer wording and the FAQ entry. Quick ask: Quicksilver's contract has a non-standard committment window (monthly minimums), so the credits calc needs to show pro-rata vs committed spend. @LegalBot can you drop the approved language?

LegalBot: Legal: "Credits will be calculated pro-rata against the customer's monthly committed spend. Credit issuance requires validation by Redwood and will be applied as a billing adjustment in the next invoice cycle." (see contract qs-2026-004).

Omar Diaz: I'll pull metrics now. Running: ```
# 30d p95 by region + 24h heatmap around peak hours
curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/summary?service=qs-onboard-api&period=30d&group=region,p95" | jq .
```
Dropping CSV and heatmap PNG to /shared/reports/quicksilver/1848524680 when done.

Ravi Menon: Note: we've seen fallback routing to ap-southeast-1 three times last 90d during a scheduler overload. Those were fast failovers but may show up in aggregate.

Omar Diaz: Uploaded metrics.csv and heatmap.png. Quick numbers: us-west-2 p95=210ms (30d), p99=520ms; uptime_us-west-2=99.89 (30d); ap-southeast-1 uptime=99.997; fallback_count_90d=3.

Hannah Liu: Draft paragraph uploaded. I framed the credit example for a $30,000 monthly commit and the contract tiers: >=99.95% no credit; 99.8-99.95% => 4% credit; <99.8% => 8% credit. Using us-west-2 observed 99.89% => falls in 99.8-99.95 -> 4% credit = $1,200. I explained pro-rata for partial-month onboarding.

Jules Park: Good. Can eng-sre confirm incident notes to include (brief bullets)? We want root cause + mitigation and whether this impacts production usage.

Ravi Menon: Short bullets: 2027-06-02 scheduler surge causing temporary queuing (mitigated by autoscaler tuning + config rollback), 2027-06-11 routing table propagation delay (fast failover to ap-southeast-1). Both labeled low customer impact by SRE.

Omar Diaz: I've added a "what we monitored" slide showing latency distribution and fallback timestamps.

Hannah Liu: I'll add an FAQ: "If you see a credit, how is it delivered?" and a simple flow for validation. Also noted that Dedicated reserved windows are excluded from standard billing adjustments and need separate handling.

Jules Park: Timeline: internal review tomorrow 11am PT, customer packet by EOD tomorrow. Ping here when slides + legal snippet + metrics CSV uploaded. Thanks team! :thumbsup:
